chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: This paper investigates the feasibility of deploying quadruped walking robots for the automation of work in roof environments. While quadrupeds have demonstrated versatility across various domains, their large-scale deployment remains limited, partly due to lack of application-specific designs. Roof environments represent a novel and unexplored use case, combining high safety risks for human workers with repetitive, strenuous tasks that could benefit from robotic assistance.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem as investigating the feasibility of quadruped robots for roof environments, matching the paper's description.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: A dedicated test rig of a roof’s surface was designed to evaluate the baseline performance of a commercial quadruped, the Unitree Go2, in this new environment.
chk_method.reason: The poster mentions the design of a roof surface test rig to evaluate the Unitree Go2 robot, which matches the paper's description of the method.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: Test rig: An adjustable test rig of a roof environment was developed using the Frankfurter Pfanne, the most common roof tile in Germany. Three core skills of the Go2 (software 1.4.4) were examined, each repeated ten times: ... while measuring slippage with OptiTrack markers at the sides of the ball feet.
chk_data.reason: The poster mentions the use of Frankfurter Pfanne roof tiles and the OptiTrack motion capture system, which aligns with both drafts of the paper's description of the dataset.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Test rig: An adjustable test rig of a roof environment was developed using the Frankfurter Pfanne, the most common roof tile in Germany. Three core skills of the Go2 (software 1.4.4) were examined, each repeated ten times: 1. Balancing: robot placed facing uphill at 0° incline, gradually increased until balance was lost. 2. Get-up/lie-down: assessed on progressively steeper inclines in three orientations (uphill, downhill, sideways); success = completing both actions. 3. Incline walking: repeated ascents of increasingly steep slopes while measuring slippage with OptiTrack markers at the sides of the ball feet.
chk_setup.reason: The poster describes the experimental setup, including the test rig, the use of Frankfurter Pfanne tiles, the OptiTrack system, and controlled trials with the Unitree Go2 robot, matching both drafts of the paper's description.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Experiments revealed that standard ball feet are inherently inadequate for locomotion on sloped roofs: slippage increased quadratically with incline angle, get-up and lie-down sequences were only possible on small inclines, and critical failures already occurred regularly on moderate inclines of 25°.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster accurately states the primary result that slippage increased quadratically with incline angle and critical failures occurred at 25°, matching both drafts of the paper's description.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Standing on incline: critical angle (27.58 ± 0.72)°. Failures were primarily caused by automatic limb repositioning, triggered by slippage of individual limbs or atypical joint angles. Get-up/lie-down: full success only at low inclines — up to 11.0° for head-up and head-down, up to 7.0° sideways. Failures occurred when the center of mass (COM) exited the support polygon during the pre-programmed motion.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster includes the critical angle for standing on an incline and the success thresholds for get-up/lie-down sequences, which align with one of the drafts of the paper's description.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: Overall, without significant modifications the Go2 is not suited for operation within roof environments. Manufacturer claims of slope-climbing up to 40° were not achieved under test conditions.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster mentions the baseline performance of the Unitree Go2 robot and compares it to the manufacturer's claims, aligning with both drafts of the paper's description.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Without appropriate adaptations, quadrupeds are not yet capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately states the main conclusion that unmodified quadrupeds are not capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments, matching the paper's description.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Limitations: the Go2 is not a high-end platform; all experiments used the standard walking gait at a single speed of 1.0 m/s (a newer ’AI walking mode’ moderately increased possible inclines in preliminary tests); all tests were conducted under ideal conditions without debris, vegetation, weather or payloads.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster explicitly mentions the limitations of the experiments, including ideal conditions without debris, vegetation, weather, or payloads, matching the paper's description.
